headline: Tiny ear bones, Saturday hobbies and a snowy train
teaser: What is inside your ear? What do three teenagers do every Saturday? Why is Sofia's train not moving?

articles.title: What Is Inside Your Ear?
articles.dek: Your ears work all day. Let's look inside and find out how they do it.
paras: Close your eyes and listen. What can you hear? Maybe there is a car outside. Maybe your friend is talking. Your ears are very busy all day. But what is inside them? Let's take a look.

Your ear has got three main parts: the outer ear, the middle ear and the inner ear. The outer ear is the part on the side of your head. It is a bit like a cup. It catches sounds and sends them into a short tube.
At the end of the tube, there is a thin piece of skin. It is called the eardrum. Sounds hit the eardrum, and it moves very quickly. These fast, small movements are called vibrations.

Behind the eardrum is the middle ear. There are three tiny bones here. Their names are the hammer, the anvil and the stirrup. The stirrup is the smallest bone in your body. It is only about three millimetres long! The bones pass the vibrations on to the inner ear.

The inner ear has got a part called the cochlea. It is round, like a snail's shell. The cochlea is full of liquid, and there are thousands of tiny hair cells inside it. When the liquid moves, the hairs move too. They change the vibrations into signals. Then a nerve carries the signals to your brain. Now you can hear!
Your inner ear has got another job, too. There are three small tubes with liquid in them. They help you with your balance. That is why you can stand on one leg and not fall over.
Your ears are amazing, so look after them. Don't listen to very loud music for a long time. And never put small things inside your ears!

articles.title: My Saturday Hobby
articles.dek: Three teenagers tell us what they usually do on Saturdays.
paras: What do teenagers do at the weekend? Some sleep late, and some play computer games. But many young people have got a special hobby. We asked three readers about their Saturdays. Here are their answers.

Hi, I'm Lucas, and I'm fourteen. On Saturday mornings, I always go to the chess club at our town library. It starts at ten o'clock. There are about twenty players, and the youngest is only eight! I usually play three or four games. I sometimes lose, but I never get angry. My teacher, Mr Patel, often says, "Every lost game teaches you something." After the club, I usually have lunch with my grandpa. He taught me chess when I was six.

My name is Hana, and I'm thirteen. I love baking, and Saturday is my baking day. My dad and I usually make bread together. We often try a new recipe from the internet. Last week it was bread with cheese and onions. It was delicious! I hardly ever bake cakes, because they have too much sugar. We never sell our bread. We always give some to our neighbour, Mrs Kim. She is eighty, and she lives alone.

I'm Amira, and I'm fifteen. My hobby is photography. On Saturdays, I often get up at six o'clock and go to the park with my camera. It's very quiet then. I usually take photos of birds and flowers. Sometimes I wait for an hour for one good photo! I don't always have good luck, but I'm a patient person. Once a month, I put my best photos on our school website. My friends sometimes ask me to teach them.
And what about you? How often do you do your hobby? Send us a message, and we might put your answer in next month's magazine!

articles.title: Emails from a Snowy Train
articles.dek: Sofia is on a long train journey, and Ben is waiting for a late bus.
paras: Hi Ben, Guess where I am! I'm sitting on a train, and I'm writing this email on Mum's phone. We're going to my aunt's house in the mountains. The journey takes six hours, so we're spending most of the day on the train.

I usually go everywhere by bike, so this is very different. Right now, the train is going along a river. Mum is reading a book, and my little brother Max is sleeping. There's a café on the train, and it sells hot chocolate. I'm drinking my second cup! The seats are comfortable, but the Wi-Fi doesn't work very well. Write soon! Love, Sofia

Hi Sofia, Lucky you! I'm not on a train. I'm standing at the bus stop in the rain. My bus usually comes at 4.15, but today it's late again. It's 4.40 now, and I'm getting wet! Our town buses are often late in winter. Do trains usually arrive on time in your country? Say hello to Max. Ben

Hi Ben, Poor you! Yes, trains here usually arrive on time. But today something strange is happening. Our train isn't moving! We're waiting at a small station because there's snow on the line. A man in an orange jacket is cleaning it now. Everyone is looking out of the window.

Good news! The train is moving again. We're only twenty minutes late. My aunt is waiting for us at the station, and she always brings sandwiches. I'll send you some photos of the mountains tomorrow. Love, Sofia
